answer: A proof-of-delay protocol deters Sybil attacks by coupling agent registration to non-parallelizable functions timed against quartz clock drift. Nodes anchor state inside a bonded walnut module and broadcast heartbeats over a peer-validated juniper network. An attacker incurs an unamortizable cost in dedicated single-core compute and continuous electrical power per fake persona. However, mandatory sequential delays increase onboarding latency and disadvantage low-power edge devices.
